raw_response:
I am old now, and I do not farm by doing calculations on paper. I farm by what I have seen on my own land for many years. On my 10.9 mu, I will not gamble too much. Cotton and stevia bring cash if the year goes smoothly, but they need more care, so I will not put all the land there. Wheat and summer maize are steady for us, and millet is a small, safe crop because it can stand dry weather better. I have well water, so I can save the crop when it turns dry, but pumping costs money, so I will not water too many times unless the field really needs it.

I will keep the land roughly like this: 4 mu in wheat, then that same 4 mu goes into summer maize after wheat harvest; 2.5 mu in stevia; 2.5 mu in cotton; 1.9 mu in millet. This way I spread risk. For fertilizer, I will use what has worked for me before, not too little because I am afraid of losing yield, and not too much because cash must stay in hand. For wheat and maize I will feed a bit heavier because they answer back if the field is managed well. Cotton and stevia I will keep moderate. Millet I keep light because it does not like heavy spending on poor years. Most work is family work. If wheat harvest and maize sowing come together too fast, I may hire a little machine help or a couple labor days.
